Biological Basis of Behaviour

The neuron, nervous system, brain structures and endocrine influence on behaviour.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the parts of a neuron and how a nerve impulse travels
  • Name the main parts of the brain and their functions
  • Explain the role of the autonomic nervous system

In simple words

Behaviour has a biological basis. The nervous system and endocrine system work together to receive information, make decisions and produce responses.

The basic unit is the neuron: it receives signals through dendrites, processes them in the cell body, and sends them down the axon. At the synapse, chemicals called neurotransmitters pass the signal to the next cell.

The neuron and impulse

Part Function
Dendrites Receive signals from other neurons
Cell body Contains the nucleus; keeps the cell alive
Axon Carries the impulse away from the cell body
Myelin sheath Insulates the axon and speeds the impulse
Synapse Gap where neurotransmitters pass the signal

A nerve impulse is an electrical wave called an action potential. It travels down the axon and triggers neurotransmitter release at the synapse.

The nervous system

  • Central nervous system (CNS) — brain and spinal cord.
  • Peripheral nervous system (PNS) — nerves from the CNS to the body.
  • Somatic — voluntary movement of skeletal muscle.
  • Autonomic — involuntary control of organs:
    • Sympathetic — fight or flight.
    • Parasympathetic — rest and digest.

The brain

Part Function
Cerebrum Thinking, memory, speech, voluntary movement
Cerebellum Balance and coordination
Brainstem Breathing, heart rate, blood pressure
Limbic system Emotions and memory (amygdala, hippocampus)

The endocrine system supports behaviour through hormones — for example, adrenaline prepares the body for action and cortisol is released during stress.

🔴 Nerve impulse direction

Impulse travels: dendrite → cell body → axon → synapse → next neuron. Myelin sheath speeds it up.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Neurological checks — limb movement, pupil response and level of consciousness reflect brain and nerve function.
  • Pain — pain signals travel through nerves; understanding pathways helps with pain assessment and relief.
  • Stress response — sympathetic activation raises heart rate and blood pressure; help the patient calm down.
  • Medication effects — many drugs act on neurotransmitters; watch for side effects.
  • Spinal injury — keep the spine still; damage below the injury loses movement and sensation.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Neuron parts: dendrites receive, cell body maintains, axon sends the impulse.
  2. Action potential is the electrical impulse along the axon.
  3. Neurotransmitters cross the synapse to the next neuron.
  4. CNS = brain and spinal cord; PNS = nerves to the body.
  5. Sympathetic = fight or flight; parasympathetic = rest and digest.
  6. Cerebrum: thought and movement; cerebellum: balance; brainstem: vital functions.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. The limbic system (amygdala, hippocampus) handles emotions and memory.
  2. Adrenaline prepares the body for action during stress.
  3. Somatic nerves are voluntary; autonomic nerves are involuntary.
  4. The myelin sheath insulates and speeds the impulse.

📌 Memory trick

Impulse direction: “DCA” — Dendrite, Cell body, Axon. Say it like “D.C.A.” or “drive carefully always”.

60-second revision

  • Neuron: dendrite → cell body → axon → synapse.
  • Action potential = nerve impulse.
  • CNS = brain + spinal cord.
  • Sympathetic = fight or flight; parasympathetic = rest/digest.
  • Cerebrum thought/movement; cerebellum balance; brainstem vital functions.
  • Limbic system = emotions and memory.

Test yourself

Which part of the neuron sends the impulse away?

Answer: C. The axon carries the impulse away from the cell body.

The fight-or-flight response is handled by the:

Answer: B. The sympathetic nervous system prepares the body for action.

Neurotransmitters are released at the:

Answer: B. At the synapse, neurotransmitters carry the signal across the gap.

Which brain part controls balance and coordination?

Answer: B. The cerebellum coordinates movement, posture and balance.

The peripheral nervous system includes:

Answer: C. The PNS carries signals between the CNS and the rest of the body.
